acceptance: The content types carry the language of passages that differ from the page locale (e.g. an optional lang field on book titles/authors and roadmap terms); components only render it, they do not decide it
On /en/, every book title and author written in Portuguese is rendered inside an element with lang="pt-BR"
On /pt/, the roadmap terms "Senior Front-End Engineer", "Full-stack ownership", "Frontend system design" and "AI engineering" are rendered inside an element with lang="en"
axe-core on /en/ and /pt/ reports no new violations compared with the previous commit, and yarn typecheck, yarn lint and yarn build pass
notes: 2026-11-24 rodada 6 (PO): PO decision on the REPORT rodada 5 review items T-025 (English terms in pt-BR) and T-026/T-027 (Portuguese book titles on /en/): keep the original text (the books are the editions read, per T-026; the roadmap terms are the job-market names) and mark the language. P1 because WCAG 3.1.2 (Language of Parts, AA) is the project bar and screen readers mispronounce these passages today.

tasks.title: Polish book progress bars for Safari and track contrast
acceptance: The <progress> element in #books has appearance-none and styled track/value for both -webkit- and -moz- pseudo-elements, so Safari shows the same rounded bar as Chrome
The track uses a design token with at least 3:1 contrast against the card background, and the computed ratio is written in the task summary
The percentage text next to each bar stays, and yarn typecheck, yarn lint and yarn build pass
notes: 2026-11-24 rodada 6 (PO): PO decision on the REPORT rodada 5 T-027 polish item. P2 because the percentage is already shown as text. The missing bar on "A Maneira Rápida e Fácil de Falar com Eficácia" depends on livros.md having a percentage and stays a review item.

tasks.title: Move focus to the section opened by a URL hash
acceptance: Opening /en/#contact or /pt/#experience scrolls to the section and moves focus to it (tabindex="-1" on the target, focus with preventScroll), so the next Tab lands inside that section
The programmatically focused section shows no focus ring, and keyboard focus rings elsewhere are unchanged
Clicking a nav link keeps scrolling to the section and also moves focus to it, and yarn typecheck, yarn lint and yarn build pass
notes: 2026-11-24 rodada 6 (PO): PO decision on the REPORT rodada 5 "Sem tarefa: T-029 e T-023" item (focus part). P2: scroll already works; this fixes keyboard and screen reader continuity.

tasks.title: Close the mobile menu on outside tap, including iOS Safari
acceptance: With the mobile menu open, a pointerdown outside the panel and the toggle button closes it, touch devices included (pointer events on document, not click)
Closing by outside tap does not steal focus when the tap landed on another focusable element, and Escape still closes and returns focus to the toggle
The listener is attached only while the menu is open and removed on close/unmount, and yarn typecheck, yarn lint and yarn build pass
notes: 2026-11-24 rodada 6 (PO): PO decision on the REPORT rodada 5 "Sem tarefa: T-029 e T-023" item (iOS part): the T-023 summary cited an outside-tap listener that does not exist in Header.tsx.

tasks.title: Keep the header on one line and tie section scroll offset to its height
acceptance: The brand "Matheus Costa Francisco" does not wrap at 1024px and 1280px in either locale, and the pt-BR nav does not overflow the header at 1024px
Section scroll-margin-top comes from a single CSS variable for the header height (no separate hardcoded scroll-mt-20), and the rendered header height never exceeds it
No horizontal scroll at 375px, 768px and 1024px in /en/ and /pt/, and yarn typecheck, yarn lint and yarn build pass
notes: 2026-11-24 rodada 6 (PO): PO decision on the REPORT rodada 5 "Sem tarefa: header" item: the header reaches ~103px in pt-BR, above the 80px scroll offset, so anchored sections land under the header.

tasks.title: Remove the stale lang="en" from #root in the pt-BR page
acceptance: pt/index.html has no lang attribute on #root and the stale "Remove the attribute in T-018" comment is gone; dist/pt/index.html exposes only <html lang="pt-BR"> as the page language
Passages marked by T-038 (lang="en" roadmap terms) keep their own lang attribute on /pt/
axe-core on /pt/ reports no html-has-lang, html-lang-valid or valid-lang violation, and yarn typecheck, yarn lint and yarn build pass
notes: 2026-11-24 rodada 7 (PO): stakeholder decision 4 (REPORT rodada 6, T-038 item marked [x]): one-line WCAG 3.1.1 fix. First in the round because every pt-BR text is announced with the wrong language until it lands.

tasks.title: Move roadmap and books to their own pages per locale with ADR
acceptance: docs/adr/0005-internal-pages.md records the slugs (/en/roadmap/, /pt/roadmap/, /en/books/, /pt/livros/), the static multi-page choice, same-tab navigation for internal pages and a 'Quando reabrir' section; ADR 0002 is not edited

src/lib exports a typed route map (page 'home' | 'roadmap' | 'books' per Locale) and a resolver from pathname to { locale, page } (unknown path resolves to the en home); no slug string is repeated outside the map

yarn build emits dist/en/roadmap/index.html, dist/pt/roadmap/index.html, dist/en/books/index.html and dist/pt/livros/index.html, each with its own <html lang>, title, meta description, absolute canonical and og:url, and hreflang en, pt-BR and x-default pointing to the equivalent page

tasks.title: Update header navigation and language switcher for multi-page routes
acceptance: On the roadmap and books pages, section links (About, Experience, ...) point to the home of the same locale with the anchor (e.g. /pt/#experience) and land on that section below the header
The Roadmap and Books nav items link to their pages (not to anchors) in the desktop nav and the mobile menu, with aria-current="page" on the current page and no target="_blank" on any internal link
The language switcher on each page links to the equivalent page in the other locale (/en/books/ <-> /pt/livros/) through the T-044 route map, and keeps the hash on the home
No horizontal scroll at 375px with the menu open or closed on all 6 pages, and yarn typecheck, yarn lint and yarn build pass
notes: 2026-11-24 rodada 7 (PO): stakeholder decision 1 (REPORT rodada 6): nav updated; internal pages open in the same tab, external links keep the new tab.

tasks.title: Add roadmap and books teasers to the home
acceptance: The home renders, where #roadmap and #books used to be (after #education, before #contact), a roadmap teaser "Studying now: <current stage theme>" / "Estudando agora: <tema da etapa atual>" linking to the roadmap page and a books teaser "Reading: <title> (<n>%)" / "Lendo: <título> (<n>%)" linking to the books page, both in the same tab

When no stage is current the roadmap teaser still renders its link without a stage name, and on /en/ the book title keeps the lang="pt-BR" attribute from T-038

tasks.title: Replace load-only entrance with scroll-triggered staggered reveal
acceptance: Sections and cards fade in with a translate of at most 16px when they enter the viewport (IntersectionObserver), staggered within a section, each duration between 200 and 500ms, using only opacity and transform; the load-only section-enter rule from T-012 is removed and no dependency is added
Content is visible without JavaScript, when IntersectionObserver is unavailable and under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (the hidden state is applied by JS only after checking both)
Opening /pt/#skills or /en/#contact leaves the target heading fully visible below the header (the hash target and everything above it start revealed, with no pending translateY)
Each element animates once (it is unobserved after reveal), and yarn typecheck, yarn lint and yarn build pass
notes: 2026-11-24 rodada 7 (PO): stakeholder decision 2 (REPORT rodada 6, T-012 item marked [x]): animation when entering the viewport, subtle, 200-500ms, CSS + IntersectionObserver. Also closes the open T-012 review item (section 12px under the header on hash links). Depends on T-046 and T-049 so their cards get the reveal.

tasks.title: Animate the roadmap journey connector and current stage marker
acceptance: On the roadmap page a connector line links the 6 stages and draws progressively with scroll (scaleY or stroke-dashoffset, no layout-affecting property), reaching full length at the last stage
The current stage marker pulses with opacity/scale only, with each motion phase between 200 and 500ms, and the status stays readable as text with aria-current="step"
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the line is drawn in full and the marker does not pulse; without JavaScript the full line is visible
Scroll handling runs through requestAnimationFrame or an observer (no unthrottled layout read per scroll event), no dependency is added, and yarn typecheck, yarn lint and yarn build pass
notes: 2026-11-24 rodada 7 (PO): stakeholder decision 2 (REPORT rodada 6, T-024/T-025 content item marked [x]): animated journey line with a pulsing current stage. Deliverables and the Method block stay as they are. Depends on T-050 to reuse its reduced-motion and observer approach.
